newsitem.title: POLAND: FORECAST - Polish 52-wk bill yield dip seen smaller.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Polish 52-wk bill yield dip seen smaller.

text.p: Banks revised up their forecasts for the average yield on Poland's benchmark 52-week T-bill, expecting it to rise to 19.63 percent by the end of 1996, a Reuters poll of the country's 25 largest banks showed.
Last month, banks saw the benchmark yield falling to 19.23 percent by year-end. At the last primary auction on Monday, the benchmark yield stood at 19.57 percent.
In December 1995, banks had expected the average yield on the benchmark paper to be 19.80 percent in December 1996.
The average yield on the 13-week T-bill was also seen rising to 18.85 percent by year-end from 18.81 percent at the last primary auction, the poll showed.
The 13-week T-bill yield forecast is a mean average of banks' predictions ranging from 18.60 percent to 19.25 percent.
Banks did not predict the level of the average yield of 13-week T-bills a year ago.
